newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Electric to raise $1 bln in bonds abroad.
newsitem.headline: Israel Electric to raise $1 bln in bonds abroad.

text.p: State-owned Israel Electric Corp plans to raise $1 billion in U.S. and European bond markets at the end of 1997 and during 1998, a company spokesman said on Monday.
The plan was approved by the company's board of directors. The board chose Lehman Brothers to lead the offering. Salomon Brothers and Goldman Sachs will act as co-managers.
The utility said its plans for 1998 require it to raise $1.5 billion.
The board also approved a credit line of 600 million marks ($335 million) from three German banks -- KFW, Societe Generale Germany and Bayerische Landesbank.
From 1992 to 1996 Israel Electric raised 980 million marks in credit lines from German banks, mainly to fund secondary power stations and to purchase gas turbines.
The company said the potential for future purchases from Germany was 900 million marks.

Israel Electric's development plans will require investments of $12 billion over the next decade and the company will continue to raise capital in the United States, Europe and elsewhere, chairman Gad Yaacobi said in a statement. -Tel Aviv newsroom, 972-3-537-2211
